processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 100 g alloy ingot melted from 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite by cold-crucible levitation melting; remelted by induction melting and poured into the rotating copper mold. As-cast steel strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm were obtained.
Stress relief annealing applied to the as-cast steel strips prior to 20% cold rolling.

Cold rolling was achieved by multipass rolling on a twin roll mill (Φ160); denoted 'CR20%'. The 20% reduction can eliminate some micropores caused by solidification shrinkage and avoid a great influence on the structure of the steel strips.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku, D/Max-2200, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, with a graphite monochromator; λ = 0.154056 nm; scanning angle 30°–100°; continuous scanning at 4°/min
characterization_methods.key_findings: For CR20% strips the constituent phases are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase, completely consistent with the as-cast strips.

purpose.value: Phase characterization of the steel strips (as-cast, annealed and CR20% conditions).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phenom Pro; after mechanical polishing and etching (3.3 vol% nitric acid, 3.3 vol% acetic acid, 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid, 3 s); photographs taken at 0.5 mm from strip surface; phase fraction measured with Image-Pro Plus (IPP) at ten different positions
characterization_methods.key_findings: The volume fraction of δ-ferrite in the cold-rolled steel strips is 5% (0Cr); cold rolling produces no significant change in δ-ferrite morphology and volume fraction; the 0Cr CR20% strip shows small isolated elongated δ-ferrite particles in the γ matrix.

purpose.value: Microstructure/phase-fraction characterisation of the steel strips.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V with a mixed solution of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips; the average slip band spacing in the CR20% 0Cr strip is 371 ± 47 nm.

purpose.value: Examine the microstructures (γ-austenite and δ-ferrite, κ-carbides, DO3 phase, slip bands) of the cold-rolled steel strips.

characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS = 1154 MPa for CR20% 0Cr; strength of Cr-containing CR20% strips exceeds that of the Cr-free strip.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; constant strain rate 2.5×10^-4 s^-1; gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm; per GB/T-228.1-2010; at least 3 tests

purpose.value: Determine mechanical properties of the CR20% steel strips.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: The measured average density of the 0Cr steel strips was 6.71 g/cm3.

purpose.value: Measure the average density of the steel strips.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP) and CS2800 carbon-sulfur analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0Cr steel (wt.%): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal.

purpose.value: Determine the measured compositions of the steel strips (Table 1).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation entanglements at the ferrite/austenite phase boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Inconsistent deformation of ferrite and austenite during deformation leads to dislocation entanglements at the γ/δ phase boundary.

interfaces.phase_evolution: After cold rolling with 20% reduction the constituent phases remain γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips.
interfaces.slip_behavior: {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips; the measured average spacing of the slip bands in the CR20% 0Cr steel strip is 371 ± 47 nm (measured at least in three different regions). The smaller the slip band spacing, the stronger the reinforcement effect after cold rolling.

phases_present.morphology: irregularly shaped; small, isolated, elongated particles (CR20% 0Cr)

phases_present.crystal_structure: BCC ordered, space group Fm3m, lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm (in the ferrite)

microstructure_list.region: 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction

structures.overall_structure: γ-austenite matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributed in the matrix; the constituent phases after cold rolling with 20% reduction are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips. {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% strip.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: ultimate tensile strength in the CR20% (20% cold-rolled) condition: CR20% 0Cr = 1154 MPa vs CR20% 3Cr = 1270 MPa and CR20% 6Cr = 1264 MPa (Cr addition increases the strength of cold-rolled strips)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times (MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm and gage length 12 mm

strain_hardening_rate.value: not quantified; strain hardening rate decreases gradually with increasing strain (lowest of the three CR20% strips)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 9(a): engineering stress-strain curve of the CR20% 0Cr strip (black curve) — lowest of the three cold-rolled curves with a plateau between the 1000 and 1200 MPa gridlines, terminating near 22% strain; Fig. 9(c): true stress-strain curve and strain hardening rate curve (dσ/dε) of CR20% 0Cr.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 0Cr (Cr-free) steel strip (Table 1, wt.%): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal. [b0017, b0018]
Measured average density of the 0Cr steel strip is 6.71 g/cm3, measured by an AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer. [b0024]

The average spacing of the {111} planar slip bands in the CR20% 0Cr steel strip is 371 ± 47 nm (measured in at least three different regions); the smaller the slip band spacing, the stronger the reinforcement effect after cold rolling. [b0066]

The strain hardening rates of the CR20% steel strips decrease gradually with increasing strain; Cr addition increases the strain hardening rate of the CR20% steel strips, so the CR20% 0Cr strip has the lowest strain hardening rate. [b0065]

A double (slip-band and microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the low-density steel strips: slip-band hardening acts at the early strain stage and microband hardening at the final strain stage. [b0091, b0099]

For the cold-rolled strips a higher density of slip bands (smaller spacing) blocks dislocation movement and increases strength, which is responsible for the higher strength of the Cr-containing cold-rolled strips relative to the CR20% 0Cr strip. [b0073]
The cold rolling with 20% reduction was achieved by multipass rolling on a twin roll mill (Φ160) and was intended to eliminate some micropores caused by solidification shrinkage. [b0023]
